body:
Source: the ADLC principle-fidelity audit (delta.md, PR #486). This ticket remediates one of the eight root-cause "seams" that audit found — cases where the toolkit trusts the model at the boundary between a built gate and the deployed system.

SEAM 5 (high). Out of the box the in-session path is advisory: --prompt-only LLM-backed gates always exit 0; rail/build-gate enforcement hides behind ADLC_*_ENFORCEMENT=1; the adversarial-review Stop hook only blocks under ADLC_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCEMENT=1. The shipped default posture is "trust the model unless the operator opts into distrust" — the inverse of the founding stance ("tool layer, not prompt layer").

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOR
1. Where the host can fail closed, make enforcing the DEFAULT. Advisory mode becomes an explicit opt-DOWN (e.g. ADLC_*_ADVISORY=1) that emits a loud, one-time notice naming exactly which enforcement was downgraded and by which flag.
2. Do not change behavior on hosts that cannot fail closed (documented per Seam 6); those remain advisory but must announce it.
3. Preserve every existing fail-closed path; this ticket only flips defaults and inverts the flag polarity, with migration notes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With no env flags set, a rail-protected edit in an enforcing-capable host is DENIED by default. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/default-enforcing.test.mjs`
- Advisory mode requires an explicit opt-down flag and emits a visible downgrade notice. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/advisory-optdown.test.mjs`
- Existing enforcing-mode tests still pass unchanged. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/*.test.mjs`

allow-suppression: none
title: Flip in-session enforcement defaults to fail-closed; make advisory an explicit, logged opt-down
